budget.rationale: The SQLite database and producer-reference ledger are bounded to a 2 GiB working set and one year of historical release evidence; retention/reclaim is performed by the scenario data maintenance command.

data.rationale: Deployment-manager owns its SQLite database and reference-ledger data under the scenario data directory.

budget.rationale: Retention enforcement receipts are bounded audit records; 1 MiB detects unexpected growth without authorizing deletion.

retention.rationale: Retention enforcement receipts preserve attributable cleanup decisions under the canonical scenario state root.

storage.rationale: Scenario-owned SQLite and evidence reference storage is declared explicitly so lifecycle startup creates the data root before opening the database.

service.name: deployment-manager
service.description: Analyzes, prepares, configures, and manages deployments of any scenario to any target platform

hostTools.name: helm
hostTools.reason: Legacy k8s deployment examples use helm template for chart rendering

redis.purpose: Optional caching layer for fitness scores and dependency tree calculations

postgres.purpose: Optional deployment inventory and migration evidence database

claude-code.purpose: AI-powered migration strategy suggestions and dependency swap recommendations (agent integration)

scenario-dependency-analyzer.runtime_only_rationale: Deployment-manager reaches scenario-dependency-analyzer through service discovery and its HTTP/Connect boundary; no source-level package import is expected.
scenario-dependency-analyzer.purpose: Dependency tree data source for fitness scoring and deployment analysis
scenario-dependency-analyzer.degraded_behavior: Deployment Manager remains available for profile and evidence review; dependency analysis and fitness scoring return an explicit analyzer-unavailable result until the provider is ready.

secrets-manager.degraded_behavior: Deployment Manager starts for non-secret deployment planning; bundle assembly that requires secret classifications returns its explicit Secrets Manager unavailable error until the service is ready.
secrets-manager.runtime_only_rationale: Deployment-manager reaches secrets-manager through service discovery and its external service boundary; no source-level package import is expected.
secrets-manager.purpose: Secret classification, template generation, and tier-specific secret strategies

scenario-to-cloud.runtime_only_rationale: Cloud deployment health is queried through the discovered scenario HTTP boundary.
scenario-to-cloud.degraded_behavior: Cloud release health checks report unavailable while scenario-to-cloud is stopped.

scenario-to-desktop.runtime_only_rationale: Desktop packaging is queried through the discovered scenario HTTP boundary.
scenario-to-desktop.degraded_behavior: Desktop packaging operations report unavailable while scenario-to-desktop is stopped.

swarm-manager.degraded_behavior: Deployment Manager remains available for analysis, profiles, releases, and evidence review; migration-task filing returns an explicit swarm-manager unavailable error until the provider is ready.
swarm-manager.runtime_only_rationale: Deployment-manager files migration tasks through swarm-manager's external Connect service; no source-level package import is expected.
swarm-manager.purpose: Optional backlog integration for approved dependency migration tasks

tier-1-local.notes: Optional accelerator that no Go code in this scenario currently opens. The declaration records intended caching, not a runtime requirement.

tier-2-desktop.reason: No vendorable cross-platform RESP server exists
tier-2-desktop.notes: The scenario does not require Redis, so the desktop tier simply runs without it rather than shipping a server.

swappable_with.notes: A durable local store behind the same Store seam preserves the durability property across restart, but not cross-replica sharing. A deployment running more than one replica still needs a real Redis.
